sections.heading: C — Vehicle checks and equipment
sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle checks and equipment

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Before driving, decide whether you are physically and mentally able to drive safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver is responsible for making sure the vehicle is safe to operate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Routine vehicle maintenance should follow the owner’s manual, with work beyond the driver’s ability handled by a qualified mechanic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Brake noise, an unusual brake smell or a brake pedal reaching the floor calls for a mechanic’s inspection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Check turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps and headlights from outside the vehicle to confirm that they work. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Brake lamps communicate that the vehicle is stopping. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
Turn signals communicate an intended turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
Using headlights during both daylight and darkness helps other drivers see the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
Have a mechanic check headlight alignment if seeing at night is difficult or other drivers frequently flash their headlights at you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
Trip planning can reduce driving by combining errands, sharing rides or using available public transportation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
Avoiding heavy traffic reduces wear on the driver and vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
Before a pickup trip, call to confirm the needed item is available or ready. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Replace damaged windshield glass because it can obstruct sight and break more easily in a minor collision or impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
Replace ineffective wiper blades so the windshield can be cleared of rain and snow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
Remove snow and ice from every window before driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distance and make turning harder on wet roads. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
Low tire pressure or unbalanced tires can increase wear and fuel use while making steering and stopping harder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side warrants a mechanic’s check. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
Worn tires can cause hydroplaning and increase the likelihood of a blowout. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
Use a gauge to check pressure while the tires are cold, using the owner’s manual to find the recommended pressure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
For the penny tread check, insert Lincoln’s head first; if the tread does not reach at least his head, replace the unsafe tire. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
Have a mechanic inspect steering that is hard to turn or does not respond when the steering wheel first turns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
Excessive bouncing or continued bouncing after a bump or stop is a reason for a mechanic to inspect the suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A02
The exhaust system removes engine gases, reduces engine noise and cools the hot exhaust. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A02
Leaking exhaust fumes can quickly be fatal and can make a driver drowsy. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A02
Do not run a vehicle’s engine inside a garage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A02
The handbook warns against sitting in a car with its engine running without an open window. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A02
Have exhaust leaks repaired when they are detected. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A02
A poorly tuned engine may lose needed power, fail to start or stall in traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A02
Secure objects on the rear shelf or back seat that could strike someone during a sudden stop or crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A02
Keep floor objects from rolling under the brake pedal and preventing braking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A02
Use the horn only to warn others. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A03
For vehicles made after January 1, 1956, the listed front lighting must be white or amber and the rear lighting red or amber, visible from 500 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A03
Headlights and taillights must not be tinted or covered with colored material unless compliant original or optional equipment meets federal manufacturing regulations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A03
High-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at 350 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A03
Low-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at 100 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A03
Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is 1,000 feet away. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A03
When overtaking another vehicle, dim high beams at 500 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A03
Headlights must be used from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A03
Headlights are required when weather or blowing dust reduces visibility below 500 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A04
Flashing or pulsating vehicle lights other than turn signals are prohibited unless the vehicle is authorized or an emergency vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A04
Decorative undercarriage lights must not rotate, flash, oscillate or use a color reserved for police or emergency vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A04
On vehicles made after January 1, 1956, turn signals must show white or amber ahead and red or amber behind, visible for 300 feet in sunlight. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F44 | anchor: A04
Signal lamps are required if the steering-post center is more than 24 inches from the vehicle’s left edge or more than 14 feet from the rear edge of the vehicle or load. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F45 | anchor: A04
Brake lamps indicate slowing or stopping. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F46 | anchor: A04
For vehicles built after January 1, 1956, brake lights must be red or amber and visible from 300 feet in normal sunlight. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F47 | anchor: A04
A vehicle made after January 1, 1956 must have white license-plate illumination visible for 50 feet behind it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F48 | anchor: A04
License-plate lighting that is not original manufacturer equipment is prohibited. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F49 | anchor: A04
The muffler must prevent unusual or excessive noise. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F50 | anchor: A04
A vehicle manufactured after January 1, 1956 must provide a rearward mirror view of 200 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F51 | anchor: A04
The service and parking brakes must control, stop and hold the vehicle for its operating loads and grades. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F52 | anchor: A04
The horn must be audible from 200 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

Misconceptions: A beam’s useful lighting range differs from the distance at which high beams must be dimmed; required equipment also depends on vehicle type.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: inspect, illuminate, secure, warn; apply each condition to its named vehicle.
Glossary: High beam; low beam; clearance lamp; gross vehicle weight; break-away brake; slow-moving emblem.
Dynamic facts: No numeric tint specification is supplied; unclear reflector applicability, mud-flap wording and warning-device details are debt rather than inferred rules.
